reason: A opens with a scene that keeps its dramatic tension all the way to the hemlock — the cup, the jailer's tears, Crito closing the eyes — and then earns its definitions from that concrete death before moving to Jebel Sahaba, so the reader has a reason to keep going. B front-loads a longer, flatter trial summary and then hands off to a second courtroom (Hayes) and a string of source discussions (Keeley, Njals saga, tribute records) that read as an annotated bibliography rather than an argument in motion. B also restates its central point — the archive records what institutions could notice — at least four separate times, while A states it once and lets the wounds, ballots and cups carry it.
